newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FIN MINISTER SEES '97 GDP OF 4.7-5.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FIN MINISTER SEES '97 GDP OF 4.7-5.2 PCT.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik on Tuesday said the government expects GDP growth for next year to be between 4.7 and 5.2 percent, in line with previous government estimates.
Introducing his budget to parliament for first reading, Kocarnik added the government forecasts average 1997 inflation to be 8.6 percent, also in line with its most recent estimates.
The government had originally forecast in its budget GDP growth of 5.4 percent, but then lowered its estimate to 5.0 percent.

Kocarnik said that the budget could be characterised "as being oriented toward investment" with a major portion being put aside to help the export policy through a 60 percent increase in the subsidies to the Czech Export Bank and the Export Guarantee Insurance Agency (EGAP).
"This should help these agencies raise their capacity to help Czech exporters work under similar conditions to those experienced by foreign competitors," he said.
Kocarnik said that with this forecast, the current account deficit should be 6.5 percent of GDP next year, up slightly from the current level of 6.0 percent.
The country posted a 1995 current account deficit of roughly four percent of GDP, which grew a real 4.8 percent.
Kocarnik added that the government expected unemployment to average 3.3 percent in 1997. The Czech jobless rate stood at 3.1 percent in August.
